SOC Tier 1 Methodology.description: SOC Tier 1 analyst playbook — alert triage, initial validation, and escalation procedures.

steps.task: Review alert in SIEM — note time, asset, user, rule name, severity
Check alert history — is this a recurring false positive?
Identify affected asset — hostname, IP, owner, criticality, location
Identify affected user account — role, department, recent activity
Check asset in CMDB/inventory — is it known? Is it in scope?
Note source IP — internal/external? Known scanner? VPN range?
Correlate with related events in SIEM — search ±30 min window around alert
Check if activity aligns with business hours and user's normal behavior
Verify with user / user's manager if activity was authorized
Check for concurrent alerts from same source — pattern of behavior?
Check threat intel feeds — is source IP/domain known malicious?
Cross-reference with change management / authorized scan schedule
Cloud alert — verify if CloudTrail logging is intact (not disabled/deleted); check GuardDuty status for the region; look for suppression filters recently created
Failed logons: Is failure count > lockout threshold? Single account or spread?
Malware alert: Hash lookup — VirusTotal, MalwareBazaar, MISP
Suspicious process: Parent-child relationship normal? Commandline benign?
Network alert: Destination in threat intel? Expected protocol for that asset?
Phishing email: Check headers, links (URLScan.io), attachments (Any.run, Hybrid Analysis)
Privilege use: Was elevated action expected? Change ticket exists?
Cloud alert (AWS/Azure/GCP): Check CloudTrail/Activity Log for source IP geolocation anomaly; is this a known service role or human account? Has MFA been used? Was API call from expected region?
Cloud IMDS / metadata alert: Is the source a known EC2/VM instance? Has the instance role been used outside the instance? Cross-check with GuardDuty UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/* finding types

Email/BEC alert: Check SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass/fail in email headers; is sender domain lookalike? Check for inbox rules created by the account (Exchange audit logs Event 4462 or Entra sign-in); verify with user
Determine: True Positive, False Positive, or Benign True Positive
False Positive — document reason, tune rule, close ticket
True Positive — escalate to Tier 2 with full context documented
Include in escalation: timeline, affected assets, indicators, initial analysis
If critical/ransomware — follow IR plan, notify Tier 2 immediately
Update ticket with all investigation steps taken
Log all IOCs (IPs, hashes, domains, user accounts) in ticket
Set proper severity, category, and affected system in ticketing system
Note time of detection, validation, and escalation (SLA tracking)
Hash lookup: VirusTotal, MalwareBazaar (bazaar.abuse.ch), Talos File Rep
IP/domain reputation: VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, Shodan, Cisco Talos, Umbrella
URL/file sandbox: Any.run, Hybrid Analysis, Joe Sandbox, URLScan.io
CVE lookup: NVD (nvd.nist.gov), ExploitDB, CISA KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities)
Email header analysis: MXToolbox, Google Admin Toolbox, EML Analyzer
MITRE ATT&CK: attack.mitre.org — search technique by ID (e.g. T1059.001)
Windows Event ID reference: Ultimate Windows Security (ultimatewindowssecurity.com)
